questions.q: The maximum value of $\left(\cos \alpha_1\right) \cdot\left(\cos \alpha_2\right) \ldots\left(\cos \alpha_n\right) . \quad$ Under the restrictions $0 \leq \alpha_1, \alpha_2, \ldots \alpha_n \leq \frac{\pi}{2} \quad$ and $\left(\cot \alpha_1\right) \cdot\left(\cot \alpha_2\right) \ldots\left(\cot \alpha_n\right)=1$ is
questions.solution:
We are given that,
$\left(\cot \alpha_1\right) \cdot\left(\cot \alpha_2\right) \ldots\left(\cot \alpha_n\right)=1\begin{aligned} \Rightarrow\left(\cos \alpha_1 \cdot\left(\cos \alpha_2\right) \ldots\left(\cos \alpha_n\right)=\left(\sin \alpha_1\right)\right. \\ \cdot\left(\sin \alpha_2\right) \ldots\left(\sin \alpha_n\right)\end{aligned}$  ....(i)
Let $y=\left(\cos \alpha_1\right) \cdot\left(\cos \alpha_2\right) \ldots\left(\cos \alpha_n\right) \quad$ (to be max.) Squarring both sides, we get
$y^2=\left(\cos ^2 \alpha_1\right) \cdot\left(\cos ^2 \alpha_2\right) \ldots\left(\cos ^2 \alpha_n\right)=\cos \alpha_1 \cdot \sin \alpha_1 \cdot \cos \alpha_2 \cdot \sin \alpha_2 \ldots \cos \alpha_n \cdot \sin \alpha_n$ [using (i)]
$=\frac{1}{2^n}\left[\sin 2 \alpha_1 \cdot \sin 2 \alpha_2 \ldots \sin 2 \alpha_n\right]$
As $\quad 0 \leq \alpha_1, \alpha_2, \ldots, \alpha_n \leq \frac{\pi}{2}\therefore \quad 0 \leq 2 \alpha_1, 2 \alpha_2, \ldots, 2 \alpha_n \leq \pi\Rightarrow 0 \leq \sin 2 \alpha_1, \sin 2 \alpha_2, \ldots, \sin 2 \alpha_n \leq 1\therefore y^2 \leq \frac{1}{2^n} \cdot 1 \quad \Rightarrow y \leq \frac{1}{2^{n / 2}}\therefore$ Maximum value of $y$ is $\frac{1}{2^{n / 2}}$.

Change of momentum = force experienced per second $=2 \mathrm{mnu}$.
